questions: How can I cancel an EastMallBuy order before the agent buys it?

Open the order and check whether the purchase has actually been placed with the merchant. Give support the order number and identify the exact line you want cancelled. EastMallBuy's policy treats an unpurchased item separately from one already bought from a seller.
What if the seller has dispatched my order but the warehouse has not received it?

Record the domestic tracking number and purchase status, then contact the agent promptly. At this stage the seller's cancellation or return conditions matter. Ask whether the package can be intercepted or whether it must arrive first.
Which costs should I check before agreeing to a return?

Ask for an itemized estimate covering the refundable purchase amount, domestic return postage and any relevant deductions. Keep the amounts in the original currency and distinguish an estimate from the final credit.
How can I show that the seller agreed to an exchange?

Save the conversation with the original item, replacement option and seller's reply visible. Confirm whether there is a deadline, who provides the domestic return label and what happens if the replacement goes out of stock.
How do I tell a warehouse deadline from a seller return deadline?

Record the date of warehouse receipt for each item and separately record the seller's deadline for the requested action. A warehouse that still holds an item may be unable to send it back under an expired seller window.
Why might the balance change before my bank shows a refund?

Find the refund destination on the transaction or support decision. An account-balance credit and a reversal to the original payment method create different records. Save the date, currency and payment reference for the route actually used.
Should I discard the shipping carton if the item is damaged?

Keep the carton, packing and labels while documenting the damage. Take an overall picture followed by closer pictures that show how the damaged area sat against the packaging. Ask what evidence is required before disposal.
What if only one component of a set is defective?

Record the seller option that defines the set and identify the damaged component. Ask whether the resolution applies to the whole set or a single piece before separating the rest or authorizing a partial return.
How do I describe a fit issue accurately?

Distinguish the ordered label, the label received, the seller's sizing diagram and your own measurement. A correct label on an uncomfortable garment is a different case from receiving a different ordered size.
What makes a warehouse photograph of a size tag useful?
Request a view that connects the tag to the actual unit. Read the size system, model marking and label text together. A perfectly legible detached tag cannot establish which garment it belonged to.
How do I check a marketplace listing before approving a purchase?

Open the seller's listing, select the actual option and quantity, and read what the price includes. Save the original option wording, listing identifier and subtotal. A title or cover photograph may describe multiple variants.
How can I compare freight estimates for a mixed parcel?
Use the same destination, items and packing assumptions for each comparison. Enter packed dimensions and actual weight with units, then check each available route's restrictions and charging method.
Can a photograph taken before sealing confirm every item in a box?

It can document visible contents and packing, but a top view may hide smaller items. Compare an itemized packing record with the picture and ask for clarification about a specific piece while the box is still accessible.
The seller used two domestic tracking numbers. How do I reconcile the quantities?
Create one row per package with its tracking number, expected units and warehouse receipt. Count units by option. A package marked delivered can contain only the first part of the seller's order.
How can I report a scratched accessory without confusing a reflection for damage?
Photograph the same area from two angles with a fixed reference point. Identify whether the mark is on the item, protective film or wrapping. Describe what is visible and what still needs inspection.
What should I check before accepting a replacement option?

Compare the seller's proposed option with the one ordered, including the model, colour code, size and included accessories. Ask how any price difference will be handled and require confirmation before the substitute is purchased.
Where are EastMallBuy's current return instructions?

Use the official Refund and Return Policy for the stage of the order and the Help Center for the support path. Recheck the live order before authorizing a return, particularly if a seller has already shipped or a parcel has left the warehouse.

articles.title: Reporting a damaged accessory to EastMallBuy: photographs that identify the problem
articles.summary: A close-up of a scratch can show a defect but leave support unable to identify the item, the stage at which it appeared or the action you want. Build a short, ordered set of observations before requesting a remedy.
sections: Start by fixing the time and place

The first question is where the accessory was when the issue became visible. Was it in a warehouse photograph, inside a parcel being opened at delivery, or already in use? The point is to preserve a timeline, not to guess immediately who caused the damage. EastMallBuy's published return and refund policy distinguishes goods held before international dispatch from cases arising after dispatch. Recording the stage accurately helps an agent find the relevant item or parcel and check which conditions apply.

Imagine a detachable buckle has arrived with a mark on its polished face. If you first notice it in a warehouse image, save that image with its warehouse entry and order reference. If you first notice it after opening the parcel, record the delivery and unpacking circumstances, including the condition of the outer box and internal protection. If the mark first appears during use, say so. Moving the date back to make a case sound stronger may conflict with earlier photographs and distract from an otherwise legitimate inquiry.
Show the entire unit before magnifying the mark

Make an overview that includes the accessory and enough of its surroundings to identify it. For the buckle, show its shape, finish, attachment points and position relative to the rest of the set. A second picture can show the disputed area. If the object is tiny, include a recognizably sized reference without covering the mark. A scale is most useful when it lies in roughly the same plane as the feature. A ruler positioned much closer to the camera can distort the apparent size.

Keep the original files or warehouse images alongside any annotated copy. An arrow pointing to the scratch can save time, but drawing directly across the defect may obscure its edges. Crop for convenience while retaining an uncropped original. When support asks for another angle, you can show how the close-up relates to the whole object. Keep personal details on shipping labels within the private support channel and avoid sharing an entire address or unrelated order history merely to identify the item.
Change the lighting to test a plausible alternative

Metal accessories, polished plastic and glossy packaging reflect their surroundings. A white streak might be a scratch, a fold in protective film or a reflection of a window frame. Place the object on a plain background and change the viewing angle, keeping the marked spot identifiable. A reflection often moves as the object or camera moves; a mark on the surface remains associated with the same physical location. Look for edges of a removable film without peeling it away if doing so could alter the return condition.

Describe the result as an observation. For example, say that a line near the left attachment point remains visible from two angles and that you have not removed the protective film. That is stronger evidence than a claim that the seller shipped a defective buckle when the film still obscures the surface. If the item is in the warehouse, ask for exactly the missing view. An instruction to photograph the same point at an oblique angle is easier to fulfil than a vague request for “better quality control.”
Document packaging as a separate object

If damage is noticed after delivery, photograph the outer carton before disposing of it, including dents, crushing or punctures. Then photograph the internal arrangement and the packaging immediately surrounding the accessory. Avoid reconstructing an arrangement you did not observe. If you moved the contents before noticing the damage, explain which part of the arrangement can still be shown and which part is uncertain. Actual packing evidence is more useful than a neat staged picture that gives a false impression of certainty.

Look at whether another object could physically contact the damaged area, but do not turn a possibility into a claim about responsibility. A buckle beside a hard case and a dented carton may be relevant observations; neither proves the exact moment of impact. EastMallBuy's policy directs buyers with delivery damage or missing items to preserve packaging evidence and pay attention to its reporting window. Read the current instructions promptly and retain material such as tape when it is required for a claim.
Match the issue to the exact option and quantity

Give the product reference, seller option and number of units involved. If the listing offers silver, black and brushed finishes, make clear which one you purchased. A factory texture shown on the brushed option may look like scratching on the polished version. Compare with the correct reference rather than a different option's promotional picture. For a set of two buckles, state whether one or both show the mark and include an overview showing the whole set.

Consider the difference between a finish discrepancy and physical damage. A listing that describes a matte finish while the received part is glossy raises an option or description question. A glossy part with a deep gouge raises a condition question. If both apply, separate them into two observations and provide the relevant evidence for each. Doing so helps the merchant respond to the actual complaint without treating a photograph of the wrong finish as proof of an unrelated scratch.
Ask for the remedy that fits the evidence

Explain whether you want an inspection, a replacement component, an exchange of the complete set or information on return eligibility. Start with inspection when the evidence cannot distinguish protective film from surface damage. If a component is clearly unusable, ask whether a replacement component is available and who would cover the relevant postage. Keep the seller's reply and any conditions, especially requirements to return all accessories. The request you make and the outcome eventually offered can differ.

As an example, if the buckle is replaceable but belongs to a bag, an isolated component replacement might avoid shipping the entire bag back. That possibility depends on compatibility and seller approval. Verify the replacement finish, attachment system and dimensions, and ask whether fitting it requires altering the bag. If the seller instead proposes a partial refund, record the amount and whether accepting it closes the case. Only agree after understanding what will happen to both the original component and the financial adjustment.
Conclude with a short evidence index

A concise support message can list the item and parcel references, the first point at which the issue was noticed, the visible defect and the requested action. Name the attachments by purpose: full set, affected component, second angle, inner packing and outer carton. Attach only the evidence needed for this case. A file named “buckle-left-edge-second-angle” is easier to refer to than several interchangeable screenshots. Retain the originals in case support needs a full view or a different crop.

A complete record does not require certainty about everything. You may know exactly which part is marked and when you first noticed it while remaining unsure whether the surface beneath the film is affected. State that uncertainty plainly. Then ask the most useful next question before the item moves or packaging disappears. The result is a case that another person can inspect and act on, with a clear distinction between what the pictures show, what is still unknown and what resolution you are seeking.

A reviewer deciding whether two photographs show the same accessory may look for a fixed feature such as a seam, screw hole or stamped mark. Leave that feature in the frame when moving closer to the damaged point. For a matching pair, place the sound piece alongside the damaged one, facing the same direction. This comparison can reveal a missing cap while still showing which piece came from the affected order.

articles.title: EastMallBuy QC and fit: distinguish a wrong item, a measurement issue and a preference
articles.summary: “My jacket is too small” can mean three different things. Separate what the seller promised, what the warehouse received and how you want the garment to fit before asking for a check or a return.
sections: Write down what the purchase actually specifies

Begin with the original seller selection and the agent's confirmed order line. Record the model, size, colour and any agreed special measurements. A note you typed but did not see acknowledged is different from an agreed product specification. Keep the original size chart or diagram if one was available at the time of purchase. The live seller listing may now show another version, and a promotional photograph of a model wearing a larger size cannot establish the measurements of the unit you ordered.

Take an illustrative order for a medium overshirt with a listed garment width of 58 centimetres. You plan to wear it over a sweatshirt. There are three separate tests: whether medium was supplied, whether the garment measures as the applicable chart describes, and whether that shape suits the way you plan to wear it. A photograph of a medium tag speaks to the first test. A tape measurement following the diagram speaks to the second. Trying a comparable garment over your sweatshirt helps with the third.
Identify a selection or fulfilment mismatch

If the confirmed order is for medium and a photograph attached to the correct warehouse item clearly shows a large label, you have a specific discrepancy to investigate. Before concluding that a seller sent the wrong item, confirm the image belongs to your actual unit, particularly if you ordered more than one size. Look for the warehouse entry and an overview connecting the tag with the garment. A detached label photo in a collection of similar shirts can easily be attributed to the wrong purchase.

Also check whether the labels use different size systems. A number on a regional conversion tag and a letter on the main sewn label can describe the same garment. If the relationship is unclear, present both labels without deciding what they mean. Ask the warehouse or agent to compare them with the exact seller option. State your preference for the next action only after the discrepancy has been confirmed. Requesting a size check is different from authorizing an exchange or accepting a substitute.
Test a suspected measurement discrepancy

Find the start and end points in the seller's chart. If chest width is measured across the closed garment from underarm seam to underarm seam, do the same. A tape across the widest visible point at a different height may produce another number. Ask that fabric be laid flat without stretching and that the tape and both endpoints appear together. A close-up of the final marking can be perfectly clear and still fail to answer whether the measurement began at zero.

Suppose the warehouse reports 56 centimetres for the overshirt while the chart shows 58. Before interpreting the two-centimetre difference, check that both refer to the same size, style, unit and method. Read any tolerance specified by the seller rather than inventing one. If the endpoints are obscured, seek a clearer view. If the method is correct and the difference persists, present the chart and the measurement side by side. This gives the seller a concrete question to assess under the purchase terms.
Evaluate personal fit separately from inspection

Your current favourite overshirt might measure 61 centimetres across the chest. Even a perfectly supplied 58-centimetre garment could feel tight over the sweatshirt you intend to wear. That does not make the warehouse inspection wrong. Record the difference between your reference garment and the seller's stated dimensions, including the conditions of the measurement. A rigid woven fabric and a stretchy knit with the same flat width can also feel different when worn. A width comparison narrows the decision without guaranteeing comfort.

Try your reference over the intended base layer and identify the actual limiting point. It might be the upper arm or shoulder rather than the chest. Compare a relevant measurement if one exists. For a drop-shoulder design, the seam position changes the interpretation of a sleeve measured from that seam. A more useful question may concern neck-to-cuff length or bicep width. By identifying what you need to know about fit, you avoid paying for or requesting another measurement that would repeat an already resolved check.
Put the facts into the right type of request

For a suspected wrong unit, quote the ordered option and the warehouse label or visible variant. For a suspected chart discrepancy, provide the chart, method and unit-specific reading. For a change of preference, say what you received and what alternative you would prefer. EastMallBuy's return policy directs buyers to stage-specific and merchant conditions. Describing the reason accurately helps support determine which conditions and costs apply. A general statement that the quality is bad obscures what remedy you actually need.

If more than one issue exists, separate them. You might receive the ordered medium but notice a torn seam and also prefer a larger size. Photograph the torn seam and explain your size preference in separate sentences. Then ask whether the seller can replace the damaged piece with the larger option and what price or postage difference would result. This avoids an exchange that resolves the seam while leaving the fit preference unanswered, or a paid size change that silently ignores the documented defect.
Compare the available resolutions in practical terms

Ask what will happen to the item, when it must move and what evidence must accompany it. An additional measurement may settle a doubt without moving anything. An exchange needs a confirmed replacement and a plan for returning the first unit. A return needs the current eligibility, packaging requirements and financial breakdown. A partial credit might leave you with an item that still does not meet your needs. Evaluate the proposed outcome against the original problem rather than accepting the first available button.

For the overshirt scenario, imagine the label and chart both check out but the buyer wants more layering room. A larger size could solve that preference if its shoulder and body dimensions are appropriate. Check the larger size's complete chart before agreeing. Moving from medium to large does not change only chest width. The back length, sleeve and proportions may change too. If the larger version solves one concern and creates another, an exchange can add cost without improving the overall fit.
Keep the final record useful for the next purchase

When the issue is resolved, record the actual received size, measured dimensions, comparison method and outcome. Save any replacement identifier separately from the original item. If you later order another colour from the same seller, recheck the size chart for that version. Do not turn a single observed measurement into a rule that every medium in the shop will fit alike. Different designs use different patterns, materials and intended ease even when they share a familiar label.

A good final note might say that the ordered medium was supplied, the width matched the seller's method, and the buyer preferred more room over a heavy layer. Another might say that the ordered medium was supplied but the measured garment differed from the chart and the seller accepted an exchange. Those are meaningfully different outcomes. Recording which one occurred gives you a better question for your next purchase and a fairer, more actionable case when something genuinely differs from the order.

Consider how the garment behaves in use as well as its measured size. A correctly measured cuff may feel tight because the fabric has very little stretch. In that case describe the fabric and your fitting experience separately from the measured opening. If the warehouse used a stretched measurement while your reference garment was relaxed, request one comparable reading before deciding which concern to raise with the seller.

articles.title: Before EastMallBuy buys from the seller: verify the marketplace offer you selected
articles.summary: An agent can receive a payment before the seller purchase is placed. Use that distinction to check the item, variant, order quantity and seller conditions while corrections are still relatively straightforward.
sections: Define the offer independently of its cover image

Start with the marketplace name, seller and item identifier, then write the exact option you intend to buy. These details identify a narrower offer than the product title. A single listing can group several materials, lengths, sizes or package combinations under one appealing photograph. If the decision depends on a particular feature, such as a removable lining or reinforced base, find the wording or picture attached to the selected option. Save the evidence where you can retrieve it after checkout.

Imagine a canvas organizer photographed with three removable dividers. One seller option describes an empty organizer, another includes the three dividers and a third sells the dividers alone. A catalogue result may display every version under one name. The question is not simply whether the organizer is the one in the photograph. You need to know which combination your selected unit supplies. Change the option and check the updated price and description before copying the listing into the agent order.
Check the seller identity and listing identifier

Compare the seller page reached from the catalogue with the seller page associated with the proposed purchase. Similar titles and shared promotional images can point to different shops. The same numeric value on different marketplaces also need not identify the same listing. Keep marketplace and item identifier together. If the original link no longer opens or redirects to another item, record what changed before selecting a similar result. Replacing a missing link is an editorial or purchase decision, not automatic proof of equivalence.

Look at the current seller page in addition to any historical QC reference. A previous buyer's picture may show that a particular option existed and looked a certain way at the time. It does not establish current stock or unchanged seller terms. If the original identifier matches but the listing now offers a revised design, document the revised option. A note stating “same seller listing, different model description” is more accurate than treating matching URLs as a guarantee that all product details remained fixed.
Read quantity rules before calculating a total

Identify whether the unit is one piece, a pair, a set or an assortment. Set the requested quantity and inspect any applicable minimum quantity or price tier. A bulk-oriented seller may show a lower per-unit amount for a different order size than the one you want. Check whether assorted sizes or colours count towards the minimum, rather than assuming that distinct options combine automatically. If the selector or checkout does not make this clear, ask before authorizing a larger purchase than intended.

Consider an imaginary offer listing one organizer at 39 yuan and a three-piece set at 105. Buying quantity three of the single organizer yields three units for 117 before other costs. Buying quantity one of the set could yield three pieces for 105, but only if the set actually contains three organizers rather than one organizer and two accessories. Read the contents before comparing the arithmetic. A lower number attached to another unit is not a lower price for the same purchase.
Verify size, material and what the photographs can establish

Open the size or dimension chart for the chosen model. Check how length and width were measured, particularly for items that open, fold or taper. For the organizer, a chart might give the exterior width while the useful internal width is narrower because of the dividers. If a specific item must fit inside, the opening dimension and position of the dividers may matter more than the overall size shown in a studio photograph. Note this requirement before deciding which option is acceptable.

Material labels also deserve careful reading. A cover photo can show texture but cannot reliably distinguish two similar fibres, verify a composition claim or tell you how a stiff insert behaves under load. Separate visible features from written seller claims and from facts you have not verified. If material is decisive, ask which specification belongs to the precise selected variant. When the answer is still uncertain, decide whether that uncertainty is acceptable instead of treating a large gallery as a substitute for the missing specification.
Review domestic delivery and seller conditions

Check the destination of any delivery charge shown alongside the merchandise. A seller-to-warehouse fee belongs to the domestic purchase, while international freight is assessed for an outbound parcel. If you are buying from multiple sellers, keep domestic charges attached to the corresponding orders. For a comparison between two listings, use the same quantity and currency and add only the delivery costs actually quoted for that scope. Record whether a total is an observed checkout figure or your own estimate.

Open the relevant seller terms while the offer and selected option are still visible. If you need to exchange a size or return an incomplete set, the merchant's conditions and the stage of the purchase can matter. EastMallBuy's policy explains that stopping a purchase before the agent places it is different from trying to reverse a seller transaction later. Save any important condition, such as the accepted components of a return, with the selection itself rather than relying on a general assumption about all marketplace sellers.
Resolve ambiguity with a bounded instruction

A useful purchase note has a clear fallback. Identify the exact desired option, the quantity and any condition that should stop the purchase. For example, ask the agent to contact you before buying if the organizer with three dividers is unavailable. This gives the agent an actionable boundary. A direction to find “something close” is less useful when multiple versions differ in size or contents and you have not said which differences are acceptable.

If the seller proposes a replacement, examine its listing or option as a fresh offer. Compare the feature that drove the original choice, the price, quantity, availability and conditions. Save the reply so that your subsequent warehouse review uses the agreed replacement rather than the first photograph. When a misunderstanding involves multiple lines, explicitly name the order lines that can proceed and the one that needs clarification. One unresolved accessory should not make the rest of the intended purchase ambiguous.
Retain the confirmation that defines the warehouse check

After submitting the order, read the confirmation rather than assuming that the intended selection survived the interface. Reopen the line and compare marketplace, option, quantity and subtotal with the saved notes. If a discrepancy appears, identify whether the agent has already placed the purchase and contact the order channel promptly. Give the exact line number and requested change. Check the response before creating a duplicate purchase intended to correct the first one.

Use the confirmed selection to define a short warehouse checklist. For the organizer that might be the specified colour, correct width and three removable dividers visible with the main item. If one detail is hidden in a folded photograph, request the smallest additional observation needed. Your marketplace verification work now serves a second purpose. It lets you tell the difference between an image that merely resembles the intended product and an actual received unit that satisfies the offer you authorized.

For an order with several variants, keep verification proportional to the possible mistake. A single listing may offer an empty picture frame beside a frame supplied with a print. A screenshot of the displayed artwork cannot resolve which one you selected. Save the option text next to the quantity, then ask the agent to confirm the inclusion if the title is ambiguous. Repeat that check for the second frame size even when the product image stays the same.

articles.title: EastMallBuy shipping estimates for a mixed parcel: when the box changes the bill
articles.summary: Two parcels can weigh the same on a scale and produce different freight estimates. Work through the dimensions of a mixed parcel, test a packing change and identify the number you actually need from the warehouse.
sources: EastMallBuy · Why shipping charges may differ
sections: Start with the packed parcel you intend to send

Imagine that a pair of shoes, a folded jacket and a small metal accessory are waiting in the warehouse. The jacket weighs less than the shoes but occupies more space. The accessory fits inside a gap beside the shoe box. If you estimate freight by adding three item weights, the result ignores both the shipping carton and the shape of this combination. Equally, adding the volumes of three separate retail cartons can exaggerate the size of the final parcel if items will be repacked together.

Make an inventory in which each row describes an item, the packaging that must stay and the protection the item needs. A shoe box needed for gifting is a requirement. A disposable sleeve around a jacket may be optional. A rigid part that could scrape a shoe needs separation even if it fits neatly in the remaining space. Once these decisions are written down, a quote can correspond to a physically plausible package rather than an optimistic number produced by removing every layer.
Work an example using actual and dimensional weight

EastMallBuy's Help Center gives an example of a route using parcel dimensions in centimetres and a divisor of 8,000. The following numbers are invented to illustrate that arithmetic. They are neither an actual order nor a promise that a route uses this rule today. Suppose a carton measures 48 by 36 by 30 centimetres and weighs 5.4 kilograms with all contents and packaging. Its external volume is 51,840 cubic centimetres. Dividing by 8,000 produces a dimensional weight of 6.48 kilograms.

On a route charging the larger of actual and dimensional weight, the starting figure would be 6.48 kilograms before any billing increments or other rules. The parcel has not physically become heavier than 5.4 kilograms. Its box occupies enough space for the route's conversion to produce a larger billing input. Check the current route card to learn how that input is rounded and priced. Knowing the larger weight alone does not tell you the exact cash charge without the tariff and other applicable conditions.
Change one dimension and see whether it matters

Consider a revised packing proposal. The shoes retain their retail box and the jacket is folded differently, reducing the carton height from 30 to 25 centimetres while keeping length and width fixed. The new volume is 43,200 cubic centimetres and the example dimensional weight becomes 5.4 kilograms. If the physical weight is unchanged, actual and dimensional weight now coincide. The reduction of five centimetres removed 8,640 cubic centimetres, corresponding to 1.08 kilograms in this example.

Those results give you a specific question for the warehouse. Can the contents fit within a height of 25 centimetres without crushing the shoes, damaging an insert or leaving a hard object pressing against fabric? Shrinking the carton only on paper does nothing. The calculation identifies an achievable target to investigate. If the smallest suitable carton is actually 28 centimetres tall, recalculate using 28. Keep the revised dimensions beside the estimate and ask whether the figures refer to the sealed exterior or the dimensions of an empty carton.
Find the point where reducing volume stops helping

For a fixed actual weight and divisor, there is a boundary volume. In the example, multiply 5.4 kilograms by 8,000 to get 43,200 cubic centimetres. At or below that volume, dimensional weight no longer exceeds actual weight under this assumed rule. With the same 48 by 36 footprint, divide 43,200 by 1,728 to find the 25-centimetre boundary height. This explains why a reduction from 30 to 25 centimetres can matter while further compression may offer diminishing freight benefit.

Suppose you could force the carton down to 22 centimetres. The dimensional calculation would give 4.752 kilograms, but a parcel still weighing 5.4 kilograms continues to be rated from at least its physical weight on this illustrative route. Compare that result with the cost and risk of more aggressive packing. If reducing height beyond the boundary compromises protection, the supposed saving may disappear before you even consider the possibility of damage. Check whether a separate size band or route limit changes the outcome before finalizing the choice.
Compare two routes without mixing their inputs

Take the same measured parcel to both route estimates. Record destination, contents, dimensions, weight, route name and quote time. Only change the route in this first comparison. A quote based on an unboxed pair of shoes and a second quote based on a boxed pair answer different questions. Make a second pair of estimates if you want to investigate the packaging decision too. This produces four intelligible comparisons rather than two attractive totals whose assumptions cannot be recovered.

Read the route terms for the parcel you actually intend to send. A route that cannot accept one component, exceeds a side-length limit or requires different packing is a conditional option. Keep the condition beside the price. If you would have to split the metal accessory into a separate parcel, include the second parcel's full quote before deciding which option is cheaper. The lowest headline price can be accurate for the route and still be irrelevant to your particular combination of items.
Keep service charges and freight in separate columns

Record any selected packing service separately from the freight calculation. The service might change dimensions, weight or both, but its price is an additional part of the total. Compare the combined amount for each proposal. If option A quotes 100 units of currency for transport and option B quotes 93 plus a nine-unit service, option B totals 102. These imaginary round numbers illustrate why the smaller transport charge need not produce a smaller final payment. Use the original quote currency throughout.

Apply the same care to reductions and coupons. Enter a discount only if it applies to the specific route and parcel you will submit. Note whether the discount reduces freight only or another part of the payment. Do not count a displayed promotion a second time if the route estimate already includes it. Leaving an unverified discount out of the working total produces a conservative budget and makes it easier to reconcile the eventual payment than guessing which of several displayed amounts is final.
Compare the estimate with the final packed measurements

When the warehouse provides the final record, compare the dimensions in the same orientation and units, then compare actual weight and route. A change from a 48-centimetre length to a 50-centimetre length may matter even if the scale reading is almost unchanged. Ask whether protecting a protruding part, keeping a retail box or switching outer cartons explains the difference. Send the original estimate and current packed figures together, identifying the one change you are trying to understand.

Your final note should let someone reproduce the decision without seeing your shopping cart. List what was packed, what protection stayed, the measured exterior, actual weight, route and total quote. Mark any unknowns, such as the final billing increment, as questions for the live route information. For the example parcel, the important finding was that carton height controlled the larger billing weight above 25 centimetres. For another parcel, scale weight or a route eligibility limit may control the entire choice. The method stays useful because the answer comes from the measured package.

When comparing two packing plans, write the contents beside each quote. A cheaper figure for a parcel without the display box answers a different question from a quote that preserves the box. Keeping those descriptions visible also gives the recipient a reliable expectation of what should arrive.

articles.title: EastMallBuy warehouse QC: how to read a size label in context
articles.summary: A sharp photograph of a tag may confirm a printed size while leaving the unit, size system or fit unresolved. Learn which details belong together before accepting a label as evidence for a shipping decision.
sections: Identify the garment the label belongs to

Open the warehouse entry for the item you want to check. Find an overview that shows the garment, then find the picture of its attached label. Check that both images belong to the same warehouse entry and order. This matters when two similar shirts arrive in adjacent order lines. An image downloaded into a general photo folder can lose the record that connected it to one shirt rather than the other. Keep the reference in the filename or case note.

Imagine you bought identical blue shirts in medium and large for different people. Both front views show the same colour and design. A close-up marked medium does not tell you which unit it describes unless the record retains that connection. Start with separate notes for the two units, even if the seller packed them together. If only one label has been photographed, record which size is confirmed and request a check on the other. Do not fill the second record by elimination when both units could conceivably be the same size.
Read all markings before choosing the relevant one

Labels can contain model codes, sizes for several markets, fabric composition, washing instructions and manufacturing numbers. Locate the marking that the seller uses for the selected option. A number beside a region abbreviation may belong to a conversion table, while a larger number elsewhere on the tag may identify the model. Read the surrounding text and orientation rather than extracting the most prominent digits. If the photo cuts off the headings above several values, ask for the complete label.

Consider a shoe label that lists several regional systems. A marking of 8 next to one system and 41 next to another may be part of one conversion printed by the manufacturer. Comparing an order for an unspecified “8” with the visible 41 establishes little until the ordered system is identified. Go back to the original option wording and seller chart. If the original selection did not name a system, explain this uncertainty instead of treating a plausible conversion found elsewhere as the seller's own chart.
Check whether a removable label and a sewn label agree

A retail hangtag can be attached to the wrong garment, and an outer bag can be marked differently from the item inside. If a discrepancy appears, determine which label each photograph shows. A picture of a size sticker on a plastic sleeve identifies the sleeve's marking. A picture of a sewn label attached to the garment gives different evidence. A wide view that includes both can make the distinction clearer without requiring multiple unexplained close-ups.

Suppose the outer sleeve reads large while the sewn label reads medium and the order specifies medium. Record all three facts. The unit may be the intended size packed in a different sleeve, or there may be another issue requiring a physical measurement. Do not tell support that a large garment was received solely because of the sleeve sticker. Ask for verification of the item, using the actual garment label and an appropriate measurement where useful. Also decide whether the incorrect packaging matters for gifting or a potential return.
Decide whether the label answers your real question

Sometimes the only question is fulfilment: did the seller send the option you ordered? In that case a clear, connected label may settle the matter. If your concern is comfort or dimensions, the tag answers less. Two medium jackets can be cut differently, and even a correctly labelled piece can fit differently from a garment you already own. State whether you need identification, measurement or a view of a particular construction feature before requesting further photographs.

For a sweatshirt, identify the dimension that would determine your decision. If chest room matters, ask for a flat measurement under the arms following the seller's method. If the concern is sleeve length on a dropped shoulder, name the endpoints carefully. Do not ask for “a photo of size” when what you need is the closed garment laid flat with a visible tape. The request for the label and the request for a measurement can both be valid, but they are not substitutes for each other.
Test a size mismatch without exaggerating the evidence

Compare four items in order: the seller option selected, the agent purchase confirmation, the marking attached to the unit and any physical measurement. Identify the first pair that disagrees. If the seller selection says medium but the agent confirmation says large, the problem appears before warehouse inspection. If the order is medium, the attached label is large and the photographs clearly belong to the correct item, the warehouse evidence supports a direct query about a wrong size.

If selection and label match but the measurement appears off, compare units, endpoints and the seller's stated tolerance. A measurement taken from the back collar edge may differ from one taken from the shoulder. A garment measured while unfastened may not be comparable with one measured closed. Give support the precise conflict rather than a conclusion unsupported by the method. “Medium label; flat width appears different from the medium chart; tape start not visible” identifies both the concern and the missing evidence.
Prepare a short request the warehouse can fulfil

A useful request names the warehouse reference, the unit and the desired view. For example, ask for one photograph showing the blue shirt and attached size label together, followed by a closer view where the printed letter is readable. If two units are involved, request separate identification for each. Alter the example to match the service actually available in your order. Avoid requesting a whole new gallery when one missing label heading or a single overview would settle the matter.

When a photo is supplied, check what it resolves before sending a second request. A clearer label may establish that the ordered size arrived but leave an external sleeve mismatch unanswered. Conversely, a full garment shot may confirm the style while the size remains unreadable. Keep the unresolved question narrow. If the warehouse cannot provide the requested view, decide whether the available evidence is sufficient for you or whether the order needs further discussion before it moves into an international parcel.
Preserve the interpretation alongside the image

Save the selected option, relevant order line, overview and readable label together. Add one sentence explaining what the evidence establishes. For instance: “The sewn label on the unit in warehouse entry A matches the medium option; the outer sleeve is marked large; physical fit has not been tested.” This record is considerably more useful than a thumbnail named “QC good” because it preserves both the conclusion and its scope.

If the evidence supports a return or exchange discussion, check EastMallBuy's current policy for the stage of the item and the seller's terms. If it supports shipping, retain the distinction between confirming the label and guaranteeing fit. At delivery you can compare the actual unit with the record and refine your personal sizing notes. A size-label photo is most valuable when you know which item it depicts, which marking matters and exactly which decision that marking helps you make.

An embroidered neck label and a removable cardboard hangtag can disagree. Photograph both in relation to the garment, then ask the warehouse to check the sewn label and any seller code against your order. A loose tag may have moved between items. If the garment itself has no permanent size marking, record that limitation and request a measurement that distinguishes the two possible sizes. Preserve the original tag and packaging while the seller reviews the discrepancy.

articles.title: How to reconcile a split EastMallBuy order by item and size
articles.summary: Match seller parcels, warehouse records and purchased quantities when tracking shows several deliveries for one EastMallBuy order.
sections: Count the things you bought

One order can produce several tracking numbers. A parcel can contain several pieces. A warehouse photograph can show several angles of the same piece. All three counts might differ even when the seller has supplied everything correctly. Start with the accepted purchase details. Write one row for each exact combination of product, size, colour and quantity. Include any seller code visible at the time of purchase. This gives you a fixed point of comparison while other records continue to arrive.

Imagine a group ordering six shirts from one listing. They buy two blue XS shirts, three blue M shirts and one green L shirt. Record those as three rows. Adding them up to six is a useful arithmetic check, yet receiving six shirts in total does not settle whether the order is complete. If the warehouse holds two blue XS and four blue M shirts, a green L is still missing and a blue M needs an explanation. Recording only the total would conceal both issues.
Follow the numbers across the domestic journey

Find the tracking numbers associated with the purchase in the order record or a seller message. Keep the spelling, carrier name and last update for each one. Ask the agent to identify the order line associated with a number if its origin is unclear. Two identical carrier numbers shown on two product rows generally refer to one package. Count distinct numbers separately from the number of order rows to which they refer.

Give the example shipments labels A, B and C on your private working sheet. Package A has a delivery scan and two warehouse photographs of individual blue XS shirts. Package B has a delivery scan and a warehouse record describing two blue M shirts. Package C is in transit and the contents have yet to be checked. The buyer can account for four pieces from the first two packages. One blue M and one green L remain open. The tracking history alone cannot tell the buyer what those last two pieces will be.
Identify what the warehouse actually counted

Look for warehouse evidence that distinguishes individual physical pieces. A flat lay of a blue shirt beside a close-up of its label can establish the appearance and size of one shirt. Those two pictures cannot establish a quantity of two. Ask for a single overview with the pieces separated or for a staff count linked to the appropriate warehouse record. Identical folded items stacked inside one wrapper can be difficult to distinguish even in a clear image.

Record counts at the most precise level the evidence supports. If staff confirm two shirts but show only one size label, mark two received and one size verified. Keep the outstanding size check visible. If a sealed multipack must stay closed for a possible return, ask what the external packaging identifies before requesting that anyone opens it. Preserve any uncertainty in writing. An incomplete count provides a better basis for a follow-up question than a confident figure inferred from the folds in a bag.
Keep an open quantity apart from a shortage

Suppose C now arrives with one green L. The group has five shirts, one blue M remains outstanding and the final known package has been received. Ask whether the seller assigned another tracking number or whether staff still have a package awaiting intake. Include the current count by option and the three known tracking numbers. With that information the agent can look for an unlinked shipment, check an intake record or approach the seller with a precise shortage.

There is a meaningful difference between an open quantity and a confirmed shortage. A delivery scan for C alongside a warehouse entry still awaiting inspection leaves its contents uncertain. A completed count from C, confirmation that all listed packages have been checked and no further dispatch reported gives the buyer a clearer case to take up. Record the time of each observation. Staff reading the conversation later then know which facts were available when you raised the question and which changed afterward.
Resolve duplicate or contradictory entries

A seller might supply a replacement tracking number after a label change. Preserve the old record, mark the relationship as unconfirmed and ask whether both numbers moved physical packages. If tracking histories share the same events, treat that as a reason to investigate. Similar dates and locations alone do not establish a relabel. A warehouse record attached twice to a shopping order creates a comparable ambiguity. Confirm how many packages staff physically received before using either entry twice.

Apply the same care to seller messages. An early message announcing three shirts in parcel B is evidence of the intended packing. A later warehouse count showing two is evidence of observed contents. Keep both entries and ask staff to check the packing slip, wrapper and order linkage. Spelling out that difference gives the agent room to locate a separated item without forcing an immediate conclusion about responsibility. Save the seller's answer beside the relevant package, including which colour or size it addresses.
Decide whether the partial order can move

If the confirmed pieces are due to travel internationally, decide whether sending them separately would hinder a warehouse check, exchange or other requested resolution. Ask for current eligibility and costs through the agent before releasing the affected items. EastMallBuy publishes return information and provides a help centre. The answer for a particular order can depend on its stage, the seller and the condition of the goods. Keep the purchase and package identifiers available when seeking that answer.

A buyer who urgently needs the XS shirts may ask about dispatching just those two. Another buyer who needs the full matching group may prefer to keep everything together while the M quantity is investigated. Both can use the same reconciliation sheet. For the first buyer it identifies exactly which pieces may be released. For the second it identifies the unresolved quantity and helps prevent a partial parcel being mistaken for the entire group order.
Close the record when the figures agree

Suppose the seller confirms that a fourth parcel contains the remaining M shirt. Add parcel D, keep the shortage inquiry open and wait for the warehouse to identify both the colour and the label. Once verified, your final rows read two of two blue XS, three of three blue M and one of one green L. If the seller instead offers a refund for the unavailable M, record two received and one refunded once the transaction is confirmed. These outcomes settle the same purchased quantity in different ways.

For a group order, share a short final statement with each participant showing the item assigned to them and any unresolved remedy. Keep the settlement records apart from the later international tracking number. A six-piece domestic order might travel internationally in two boxes or five physical pieces might travel after one refund. When those boxes arrive, the recipient can compare each one with its actual dispatch list. That final list also explains why the parcel in hand contains a different number of shirts from the original purchase.

If two people share the same size, assign individual pieces only after the common size row balances. Marking one blue M shirt for each person too early can create the impression that everyone has received a shirt even when only two exist. Keep the physical count beside the assignment list and name the person who checked it. That small distinction matters when a fourth package arrives after the initial allocation.

articles.title: Keep, fold or discard? EastMallBuy packaging decisions before a return
articles.summary: Removing a retail box can make an outbound parcel smaller. It can also remove the product's protection, identification or evidence needed for a return. Decide what each layer does before sending disposal instructions.
sources: EastMallBuy · Why shipping charges may differ
sections: Identify the layer you are talking about

A request to “remove the box” sounds precise until you unpack the word box. A single delivery can arrive in a seller's shipping carton, a printed retail carton, a moulded insert, a fabric bag and a protective sleeve. Only some of these layers may affect the product's resale condition or the seller's acceptance of a return. Others may be expendable after intake. Give each layer a name and, if the location is unclear, use a photograph with the relevant part indicated.

Picture a pair of glasses arriving inside a hard case. The case sits in a printed presentation sleeve, itself wrapped in plain protective cardboard. Removing the plain outer delivery box is different from throwing away the hard case. Even removing the presentation sleeve could matter if the seller's listing includes it as part of a gift set. Before requesting a change, compare the selected option and purchase description with the layers actually shown. Record which items were sold as contents and which materials merely protected them in transit.
Decide whether the purchase is settled

Read any outstanding questions attached to the order first. Is the quantity correct? Has anyone checked the colour or size? Are there scratches, missing pieces or a pending exchange request? When the purchase is still under review, the value of retaining packaging can extend beyond protection. The retail label may connect a disputed unit to its seller option. The packing arrangement may help explain the condition in which the item arrived. Discarding either source of information can make the later discussion harder.

EastMallBuy organizes its return policy by stage. Once a seller has received a purchase or the warehouse has received the goods, the applicable merchant terms and order circumstances matter. Ask whether the relevant seller requires packaging, labels, inserts or attached tags for the requested remedy. Keep the answer with its order reference. A comment about another seller's return approval does not establish what this seller will accept. If the answer is still pending and disposal would be irreversible, leave that layer intact while clarifying your options.
Compare protection before comparing dimensions

Examine how the current package restrains the item. Does a stiff insert support a delicate handle? Does the inner case prevent pressure on a lens? Does the retail box keep two surfaces from rubbing together? A smaller parcel that removes those functions has changed more than volume. Describe the protective job in practical terms before deciding whether another material can perform it. Two objects that fit in the same physical space can still damage one another if the parcel moves.

For the glasses example, suppose the hard case is staying. The presentation sleeve adds little padding, while the plain carton prevents the hard case from moving against a metal accessory. If the outer carton is removed, you still need a way to separate that accessory. If the case itself is removed, you need to consider pressure on the frames and lenses, not just surface scratches. Ask about available repacking choices and their dimensions rather than writing an instruction that leaves the warehouse to infer which risks you accept.
Measure the saving at the parcel level

EastMallBuy's freight help explains why dimensional weight can make a large parcel cost more than another parcel of equal scale weight. Measure the proposed outer parcel, not just the retail box you hope to remove. If the longest side of the international carton is set by another item, folding one small box may save almost no billable space. If one empty retail box determines the carton height, changing it may materially affect the quote. The external carton is the object the route rates.

Use a fictional case to see the distinction. A presentation box occupies 28 by 20 by 10 centimetres, but a rigid item beside it already requires a parcel 30 centimetres tall. Removing the presentation box may create an internal gap without reducing the exterior at all. Conversely, a retail lid that sticks up just two centimetres above every other item might require a taller carton. Record the proposed external dimensions and packed weight for both versions. Ask for the route calculation applicable to the actual destination and contents.
Specify what should happen to the saved components

Sometimes the choice is to fold and retain the retail carton. State whether flattening is acceptable, whether the lid or sleeve should remain assembled and where the loose item should be placed. A collector or gift recipient may care about creases; another buyer may only need the printed model label. Decide which feature matters before asking for a change. If the original carton uses a glued or rigid construction, folding may not be possible without damaging it, however easy a rectangular diagram makes it look.

Write a short instruction such as: keep the hard case and cloth; retain the labelled presentation sleeve flat only if it folds along its existing seams; remove the plain seller delivery cardboard after recording the label; keep the metal accessory separately wrapped. This is an example of the level of detail, not a service promise. Check what the warehouse can actually do. If it offers a simpler set of options, choose the available option that meets your requirements or ask one question about the specific exception.
Document the condition before and after the change

Keep an overview showing the item and its original layers together. Save close pictures of existing dents or tears if they may be relevant to an open case. When a seller label is important, record the model or option marking as well as a readable image. A detached photograph of a label without its connection to the unit can be ambiguous. Keep personal delivery details out of any imagery you share outside the order's private support channel.

After repacking, check the result against the instruction. A sealed parcel photograph might confirm a changed exterior but reveal nothing about whether the cloth or hard case remained inside. If the presence of those items is essential, ask whether an appropriate view or packing record is available before the parcel is sealed. Do not confuse a request being accepted with the requested arrangement already being verified. The order evidence, warehouse response and final packing state represent different pieces of information.
Close the decision with an actual comparison

Compare the two complete proposals, including packing service charges, the current route estimate, retained protection and effects on a possible return. If the smaller parcel saves little and the seller has not yet accepted the product, waiting or keeping the packaging may be the sensible decision. If the unit has been checked, the seller's requirements are understood and the package can be safely reduced, a clearly specified removal may be reasonable. The right choice depends on this item and its route.

Record the choice and why you made it. For instance, retaining the glasses case protects the product, retaining the printed sleeve preserves the option evidence, and removing only the large outer carton reduces the parcel footprint if the revised measurements confirm it. This explanation gives you something concrete to verify at dispatch and upon delivery. It also prevents an instruction written for a soft garment or disposable carton from being applied indiscriminately to a fragile item or a product still under review.

Keep loose inserts identified when two boxes look alike. A small paper sleeve or spare component may fit either box while its printed model number belongs to only one. Photograph the layout before separation and place each item's inserts back with its matching model number when preparing the return.

articles.title: EastMallBuy returns before dispatch: find the right stage of your order
articles.summary: A payment, a seller shipment, warehouse receipt and an international waybill are different events. Identify which one has actually happened before asking EastMallBuy for a cancellation, an exchange or a refund.
sections: Read the order line before the parcel record

Suppose you have bought a jacket and a bag from different sellers. The bag arrives quickly. You notice that the jacket order lists the wrong colour and would like to change it. A dashboard may show that you have one item in storage and money already committed to another. Neither fact tells you whether the jacket seller has received the purchase. Open the jacket line itself. Read the selected option, the purchase status and the time of the most recent change. If there is a seller tracking number, keep that number with the item.

The distinction matters because EastMallBuy publishes a staged refund policy. Broadly, an instruction to stop an unplaced purchase is different from a request to unwind a purchase already made with a merchant. An outbound shipment adds a separate decision about logistics. Treat the current order status as the starting observation and the policy as the map for choosing a request. A friend who received a refund in a different situation cannot tell you which stage your own item has reached.
If the agent has received payment but has not purchased

Gather the order number, selected item and quantity. Check for an update that the merchant order has actually been placed. If the intended purchase is still waiting, tell the agent which line you want stopped. If you simply ask to cancel “my order” when several lines exist, a member of support may need to ask which items you mean. Quote the relevant line and explicitly state whether the rest of the purchase should go ahead. Save the message and the time you submitted it.

For the jacket example, a precise request would identify one medium jacket in the wrong colour and say that the bag should continue through the normal process. If you would prefer a replacement colour, decide whether you are authorizing a substitution at an agreed price or asking for cancellation so that you can order the correct item separately. Those are different instructions. Wait for confirmation of the original line's disposition before paying a second time for the same intended purchase.
If the seller has already received the purchase

Look for the actual marketplace order stage. A purchase can be placed without a tracking number yet being available. It can also be on its way to the warehouse even though the warehouse inventory screen is empty. EastMallBuy refers to merchant and marketplace conditions for this part of the process. Collect the seller listing and option text that existed when you paid. An edited listing may no longer show the exact version supplied under your purchase.

Explain the reason for your request in terms that can be checked. “I chose charcoal and now prefer beige” and “I selected charcoal but the seller confirmed beige” suggest different conversations with the merchant. Include the selection or message that establishes the difference. Ask for the seller's reply and what must happen next. An agent's acknowledgment that the question was sent is a progress update. An actual seller agreement should identify the item, the requested resolution and any conditions attached to it.
If the product is already in the warehouse

A warehouse entry gives you evidence that did not exist when the item was still with the seller. Link the entry to the order number and inspect the supplied photographs. Save the most informative view and an overview that identifies the unit. If the issue is a size mismatch, a photo of the attached size label may be enough to ask a focused question. If you believe a bag strap is missing, ask whether it was packed inside the bag before treating the omission from a photograph as proof.

Decide what you need done while the item is physically available. Request a check or return before including it in the next parcel. Keep the seller's original packaging if it may be required and ask about domestic return postage. Open the current policy and order-specific terms as soon as the issue appears. Do not use the length of the warehouse storage period as a calendar for making a return decision. Storage, merchant acceptance and an individual after-sales request each concern a different action.
If an international waybill already exists

Find the waybill number as well as the purchase number. A waybill can exist before a parcel leaves. Conversely, an older screen can make a parcel look as though it is still editable after packing has progressed. Ask specifically whether dispatch can still be stopped and whether the particular item can be removed. If the request affects only the jacket, give its warehouse entry and say what should happen to the unaffected bag. Do not assume a change to the product order will automatically stop the parcel.

Work through the cost implications of the proposed change. The product amount belongs to the seller transaction. Outbound freight belongs to the international shipment. A warehouse service already performed is a third line. Even when staff can stop a parcel, the amounts associated with those lines can be treated differently. Ask for the breakdown in writing. The old estimate for a parcel containing two items may also need updating if one is removed and the packing changes.
Track the money with the same precision as the goods

Make a short reconciliation record with four fields: original charge, expected refund, actual credit and destination. Record currency as well as amount. A quote given in yuan and a card statement in euros cannot be compared as bare numbers. Keep the reference for each transaction and check whether the case concerns a merchant refund, return postage or a separate withdrawal of an account balance. These may appear in different places and on different days.

For an illustrative purchase of two units at 80 yuan each, returning one unit starts with an 80-yuan item value. It does not automatically establish either the final credit or a refund of half the full international parcel cost. Add any agreed postage or deduction only when the agent or merchant identifies it. If the expected credit is 72 yuan after an explained eight-yuan deduction, compare the final credit with 72 and keep the explanation beside it. These figures demonstrate the arithmetic and are unrelated to EastMallBuy's actual fees.
Close the loop before moving the remainder

A resolved case should answer three questions. What happened to the physical unit? What amount went where? What can the warehouse now do with the remaining products? If the seller accepted an exchange, wait for a replacement identifier or incoming unit and check its option again. If the order was cancelled, keep the confirmation with the payment record. If a combined parcel had to be reopened, review its revised contents before authorizing shipment. Archive the original evidence once you have an outcome for each item.

There is value in writing a short case summary even for a small purchase. “Wrong colour found before seller dispatch; merchant cancellation confirmed; expected credit recorded; bag remains in warehouse” contains more usable information than a folder of unexplained screenshots. Someone reading your message can identify the next action without reconstructing an entire chat history. If facts change, revise the stage and the affected references first, then consult the part of EastMallBuy's live policy that applies to that new situation.

If the order contains a matching pair, clarify whether the seller expects the entire pair back. Sending only the visibly defective piece might leave the return incomplete. Ask the agent to record the required quantity and any included accessories before a domestic return label is used. This also gives you a count to check against the eventual settlement.

articles.title: Reviewing an EastMallBuy parcel before dispatch: contents, protection and instructions
articles.summary: An international waybill groups several purchases into one movement. Check which units will travel, how they will be protected and which measurements support the shipping choice while corrections may still be possible.
sources: EastMallBuy · Why shipping charges may differ
sections: Establish the contents before discussing the box

Make your own packing list from the warehouse entries you intend to submit. Include order reference, unit, option, quantity and whether each item has completed the checks you need. If one piece is awaiting a size confirmation or seller reply, leave it explicitly marked as pending. A parcel record can appear complete while containing an unresolved item. Equally, a shipment of several items may accidentally leave behind a small accessory if its warehouse entry is easy to overlook.

Imagine a parcel containing two folded shirts, a pair of shoes with a retail box and a small ceramic pin. The decision is not simply whether four purchase lines appear. Confirm that both shirts have the correct labels, the shoes form one matched pair and the pin is included as a physical component. If the pin came packed inside one of the shoe boxes, decide where it should be during international transport. A small item hidden inside another package can be both overlooked during inspection and vulnerable to contact damage.
Give each protection instruction a clear purpose

Describe the risk you are trying to control. For the shirts, moisture or transfer of colour may matter. For the shoes, crushing or deformation may matter. For the ceramic pin, impact or pressure on a small point may matter. Explain how the objects should be separated if one can damage another. A generic request for “extra protection” leaves the packer deciding whether the priority is stiffness, cushioning, waterproofing or minimizing empty space. Different priorities can imply different packing materials.

Be clear about seller packaging. Keep a retail box if the box itself matters or helps protect the item. If you would accept folding or removing a layer, state exactly which one and check any open return conditions first. A request to remove “all packaging” could remove tags, inserts or protective sleeves you intended to retain. Ask which service is available for this parcel and what it changes. A service's name alone may not explain which components it affects or whether its effect is reversible.
Check the physical arrangement where evidence is available

An open-carton photograph, if available, can answer useful questions about arrangement. It may show the shoe box beneath another item, the pin wrapped separately or a gap that lets contents move. A closed-carton photograph answers different questions about the outside, visible sealing and carton condition. Decide which view supports the concern you have. A closed box with clean tape cannot establish that a specific shirt or small pin is inside, however reassuring the external appearance looks.

If an open view shows only the top layer, do not claim the lower layer is missing. Compare the warehouse entries and packing list, then ask about the specific unseen item. For the pin, useful evidence might be a picture of the wrapped pin next to its labelled pouch before the pouch enters the carton. If such a check is not available, keep that limitation in your records and decide whether the packing arrangement is adequate. Avoid asking the warehouse to unpack a sealed parcel unless the unresolved issue justifies it.
Match packed dimensions with the intended route

Read the external length, width, height and scale weight associated with the current packing arrangement. If you authorized a different carton or removed the shoe box, figures recorded before that change may be stale. EastMallBuy's freight help explains that dimensional weight can affect a charge. Use the current route's conditions and the measured completed parcel, not measurements of individual seller boxes or an estimate copied from a different destination. Keep units visible and record the time of the quote.

Check eligibility separately from cost. An inexpensive route can have restrictions involving dimensions or contents that make it unsuitable for this parcel. If a particular item would require splitting the shipment, obtain comparable quotes for the split arrangement before assuming the lower route price saves money overall. Compare the actual destinations, packing options and services. A valid comparison includes both parcels if two are required and includes the packing protection you have decided to retain, even if that produces a higher total.
Read the outbound instruction as the warehouse will see it

Check the recipient and destination in the actual submission screen. Confirm the address, postal code and contact information privately in the service, particularly if your account contains more than one saved destination. Ensure the selected route corresponds to that destination and to the packing assumptions in your quote. Do not paste private address details into public photo-review groups when asking an unrelated question about carton protection. A cropped view or a simple description of dimensions can be sufficient for that discussion.

Read any special instructions from the perspective of a packer handling several similar items. “Keep this box” is ambiguous if the order has two cartons. “Keep the shoe retail box for warehouse entry A; remove only the plain outer seller shipping carton for entry B” provides a usable mapping. If you revise the instructions, identify the replacement version and ask whether packing has already started. Adding a second conflicting instruction without withdrawing the first can create precisely the uncertainty you wanted the note to resolve.
Understand the stage at which you are requesting a change

Creating a waybill and physically dispatching a parcel are different events. EastMallBuy's policy treats the period before international dispatch separately from the period after it. If you notice a problem, give support the waybill reference and explain the requested change immediately. Ask whether the parcel can still be stopped or amended, what service has already been performed and whether the estimate must be revised. Do not assume an uncollected or unscanned tracking number proves that packing can still be reversed.

Suppose the ceramic pin is discovered to be missing from the intended set just after parcel submission. Your request should say whether you want the whole parcel held, the pin checked or the unaffected items dispatched without it. Ask which option remains physically possible and how it affects charges. Save the answer and the actual outcome. A product-level discussion about replacing the pin does not automatically suspend an international waybill that has already entered processing.
Save a release record you can use on delivery

Before considering the parcel ready, keep the accepted packing list, final instructions, route, dimensions, weight, amount and waybill number together. Record any item intentionally left behind. Save relevant pictures of condition and protection, separating seller or warehouse reference photos from pictures of this actual packed parcel. A later support inquiry is easier when you can point to one outbound reference and identify the individual unit inside it.

At delivery, compare the package and contents with that record before disposing of packaging, especially if you see damage or missing pieces. Follow the current carrier and EastMallBuy reporting instructions for the situation. A good pre-dispatch review cannot guarantee safe delivery, but it makes three important facts recoverable: what you authorized to travel, which protection you asked for and what the warehouse actually documented. Those facts are useful whether the parcel arrives perfectly or needs an after-sales investigation.

A useful final message describes the receiving end as well. If the recipient needs to identify two wrapped gifts separately, ask whether removable outer labels can distinguish them without marking the retail boxes. Use short descriptions that still make sense to someone who never saw the shopping cart. A label identifying the blue ceramic mug and another identifying the cream mug will remain meaningful after the warehouse reference numbers have been covered by protective wrapping.

articles.title: EastMallBuy exchange requests: turn a seller's reply into a usable agreement
articles.summary: A seller saying “yes” is only useful if you know which unit will go back, what will replace it and what happens to the money. Capture those details before the warehouse acts on an exchange request.
sections: Describe the change in one complete line

Begin with the line on the paid order. Suppose you ordered a navy zip jacket in medium, the seller sent black, and you would accept navy in the same size. Your change request should identify the item reference, the option ordered, the option received and the exact replacement you would accept. If you ask for “the right one,” everyone handling the case must recover the original context before making a decision. If you say “any navy is fine,” you may accidentally accept a different model or fabric.

There is another important possibility. You received the navy medium as ordered but would now prefer a large. That is a different reason for an exchange. Describe it accurately. EastMallBuy's published policy distinguishes stages of a purchase and directs the buyer to merchant or marketplace conditions for a number of return decisions. The reason and timing can matter to the discussion of costs. A precise statement helps the agent present the actual case rather than a stronger-sounding complaint you cannot support with evidence.
