Identify the party who answered and the action they approved

A conversation can contain several confirmations that look alike. The agent may confirm that your message was received. The warehouse may confirm that the jacket is still available. The merchant may confirm stock of the navy medium. None of those individual statements necessarily establishes that the merchant agreed to take back the wrong unit on the terms you expect. Keep the question and the relevant reply together, including any wording that limits the answer.

For example, a reply saying “medium available” answers a stock question. “Return this black medium with its tags; we can exchange it for the navy medium from this listing” identifies a physical return and a proposed replacement. Even this second reply may leave the deadline and domestic postage unresolved. Use it as evidence for the portions it actually answers. If translation makes the reply ambiguous, preserve the original text and ask the agent to clarify the unresolved point before instructing anyone to send the jacket away.
Record the identity of the replacement

Write down the replacement listing identifier and variant wording. If the replacement comes from the same listing, compare all selectors rather than just the one you intend to change. A colour change might reset the size or alter the material options. If the merchant proposes another listing, open it and check model, construction, quantity, size chart and price. A similar studio image offers little protection against accepting an entirely different version of the jacket.

Make a small acceptance record with an “existing unit” row and a “replacement unit” row. Both should state marketplace, seller, listing, colour, size and units included. Record an unknown value as a question rather than copying it across automatically. In our example the replacement must be navy, medium, single jacket, same model and same fabric. If the seller instead offers a navy large because medium sold out, the form makes the proposed substitution obvious and gives you a clear decision to make.
Establish what must go back and when

Ask what the merchant expects to receive. For a jacket that might include the item, attached tags, removable belt and seller packaging. For a set it might be the complete set even if only one component is disputed. Separate the seller's retail packaging from the warehouse's international shipping carton. When the seller requests “original box,” ask which one is meant if more than one box exists. Photograph the return contents together before sealing where the available service permits.

Next identify the effective deadline and the action that satisfies it. A requirement to open a case by a date differs from one to dispatch a return or have the merchant receive it by that date. Do not infer the requirement from a calendar reminder alone. Save the seller or platform wording, its time zone if stated and the last confirmed action. If the timeline is short, ask for an immediate answer about eligibility while the item is still in the warehouse.
Agree how postage and price differences will be handled

Create separate entries for the old item amount, new item amount, domestic return charge and any reshipment or handling charge that is actually quoted. Ask who pays each amount and when. Do not enter an anticipated seller reimbursement as money already received. If the replacement costs more, specify whether you approve the difference and the currency. If it costs less, ask how the difference will appear. Keep the agent's answer next to the originally agreed figures.

Consider an invented example. The original item costs 120 yuan, the proposed replacement costs 128 and there is a quoted domestic return charge of nine yuan. Before any other conditions or reimbursement, approving those two additional amounts would imply 17 yuan of further cost. If the seller agrees to cover the nine yuan later, your initial outlay and eventual net cost may differ. Record both. These numbers illustrate reconciliation and do not represent EastMallBuy rates, seller policy or a guaranteed outcome.
Trace the return and the replacement separately

When the item moves, keep the outgoing domestic tracking record attached to the old unit. Save the warehouse release date and any receipt or merchant acknowledgment. If a replacement is dispatched, attach its tracking number to the new unit. Reusing a single generic field called “tracking” causes problems when both shipments are in progress. A delivered scan on the return can mean the seller has received the old piece, while your replacement has not yet left their shop.

Plan for an interruption. What if the seller approves an exchange, receives the return and then reports that the navy medium is unavailable? Retrieve the accepted replacement description and any contingency agreed earlier. Decide whether you prefer a refund, a fresh wait for stock or another specifically identified option. Make the new choice explicit. A warehouse team that knows you agreed to one alternative should not have to guess whether you will accept a second, materially different proposal.
Inspect the replacement before closing the case

Match the replacement warehouse entry to its order or exchange reference. Compare the new photographs with your replacement row. Check the changed feature first, then make sure features that were supposed to remain the same still match. In our example that means checking the navy colour and medium label on the same unit and verifying that the jacket still uses the agreed zip and fabric. A picture inherited from the old warehouse entry cannot answer those questions about the replacement.

Finish by checking the financial side as well. Mark outstanding postage, top-up or credit entries as settled only when you can identify their transaction records. Your final case note can be brief: black medium returned under the recorded domestic number; seller acknowledged receipt; navy medium arrived under a new warehouse reference; replacement checked; agreed difference posted. A note like this resolves both the movement of goods and the movement of money. It also leaves the correct unit ready to include in your later international parcel.

When two options look similar, preserve the exact seller wording for the replacement. A message agreeing to send a darker version can leave room for disagreement if the listing contains navy, charcoal and black. Ask the agent to repeat the replacement code or colour name back to you. Add that confirmation to the original purchase record so the second warehouse inspection checks the newly agreed variant, even if the first order line continues to show the original colour.
